method: This curated ledger records named changes already merged into the project, not every Git commit or a claim of historical accuracy. A feature release records software and editorial delivery, not specialist review. No public correction records have yet been documented. Zero correction records does not establish that the archive is error-free.

roles.label: Maintainer and release editor
roles.description: Responsible for approving public updates through GitHub; a release commit does not constitute independent historical review.

roles.label: Subject editor
roles.description: Future role for section-specific historical, manuscript, biblical, linguistic or diaspora editorial decisions.

roles.label: Independent specialist reviewer
roles.description: Requires an identified, qualified person, documented scope, date and assessment before a completion claim may be displayed.

roles.label: Community testimony and rights custodian
roles.description: A future responsible person or institution needed before accepting private interviews, releases or restrictive material.

changes.title: Explore topic categories - startup fault and browser filter regression
changes.summary: Fixed a JavaScript initialisation error where querySelector('.search-open') was treated as an iterable with .forEach(), preventing the rest of the page's JavaScript setup, including all Explore topic filters, search, sort and reset controls. Corrected the search trigger binding using querySelectorAll, aligned results labels with reading entries, and added a comprehensive real-script Node VM regression suite exercising all six topics, homepage ?topic= links, invalid topic values, search/category intersection, sorting, empty state, counts and reset. The new test runs in standard validation CI. Patch-level usability correction; source records, historical claims and content were not changed.
changes.impact: Restores functioning Explore category buttons under the search bar, along with the header search trigger and related page controls. Root and GitHub Pages subpath builds and all automated regression tests passed before merge. Automated browser simulation does not substitute for manual Safari, touch and assistive technology testing.

changes.title: Ancient Kaldu lineage evidence: historical proof requirement
changes.summary: Revised the source-critical guide, Assyrian identity article, Chaldean Catholic Church entry and linked Christian tradition explanations to state explicitly that no ancient-to-modern Kaldu ancestry or discrete ethnicity for the present Chaldean Catholic community is demonstrated in the archive's cited primary record. The evidence finding is NOT DEMONSTRATED, rather than a conjecture treated as an equally evidenced alternative to documented East Syriac, Church of the East and Assyrian communal inheritance. Recorded present-day self-descriptions as contemporary observations only, not proof of ancient descent. Added Elizabeth E. Payne's independent ancient-history reference, updated the provenance limits for Coakley, Hanoosh, Iranica and Donabed, expanded three individually mapped evidence sections and registered three additional anchored unreviewed claims CL-089 to CL-091. Curated sources are now 139; mapped evidence trails 379; claim queue 91.
changes.impact: The question of ancient ancestry is evaluated against positive dated records rather than denominational dogma, reuse of an ancient name or modern identity preference. The ancient Kaldu of southern Babylonia and later northern Mesopotamian Chaldean Catholic ecclesiastical identity have distinct source histories. A bounded absence of demonstrated evidence is not a global genetic finding, a prohibition of contemporary self-identification or an assertion that every possible archive has been reviewed. Independent Assyriological, early-modern archival and ethnographic specialist review remains outstanding.

changes.title: Chaldean Catholic church designation and shared Assyrian heritage: independent identity sources
changes.summary: Substantially expanded the Assyrian identity, Syriac church traditions and Chaldean Catholic Church essays; added a ten-section source-critical guide distinguishing church communion from ancient ethnic descent, ancient Babylonian Kaldu, nineteenth-century ethnic naming debates, Assyrian cross-denominational heritage and present-day self-identification. Added seven independently attributed scholarly, ancient-history and institutional references bringing curated sources to 138. Explicitly labelled Chaldean diocesan and CNEWA material as church institutional testimony, not independent ethnicity evidence. Maintained 29 mapped sections across four identity essays, bringing total section reading trails to 376, and added eight anchored, pending expert-review claims CL-081 to CL-088 bringing the claim register to 88. Linked guide from Explore's balanced columns and added source-provenance regression tests.
changes.impact: Chaldean Catholic is firmly identified as a church affiliation; that affiliation is not proof of an ancient ethnicity or separate language. The article records that modern ethnic self-identification and scholarly disagreement also exist, and does not assert anachronistic late-1990s invention, unbroken descent from ancient Kaldu or unsupported malevolent motives. Independent evidence types and incomplete journal/book access are disclosed, and no named independent specialist review has occurred.

changes.title: Exile, resettlement and provincial life - primary source strengthening
changes.summary: Published twelve source-typed studies with seventeen biblical reading routes and thirteen distinct supporting reference identities across five research categories, plus seven new institutionally catalogued primary and academic records. Added one directly identified Samarian grain-tax letter SAA 1 220/P334789, preserved separate original royal records and museum visual objects, and gave specialist-only citation status to the Aramaean logistics and household letters SAA 19 17-18 and later Guzana name references SAA 16 63. Expanded the existing Assyrian exile dossier by seven substantial sections and Samaria by one, linked eight additional section reading trails and eight pending original claims to the source and evidence registers. The curated source library now has 131 maintained records; the awaiting-independent-review queue has 80 anchored claims.
changes.impact: Scripture remains primary evidence for biblical passages and stated destinations; ancient letters, royal inscriptions and reliefs are direct evidence only for their own claims and materials. Halah-Halahhu and Guzana/Habor interpretations remain historical geography, the Medes' provincial dates remain conditional reconstructions, and Aramaean letters or later Judah reliefs are not misattributed to Israelite deportee groups. Original-language collation, ancient population ancestry assertions, full Oxford chapter audit, real-device interactions, cartographic verification and named independent specialist review remain pending.

changes.title: Balanced global navigation and automatic desktop hover dismissal
changes.summary: Reorganised the growing Research menu into three grouped desktop columns, Explore into two, with two-column medium screens and stacked mobile disclosure sections. Fixed selection of only the first native details group in shared JavaScript, implemented mouse pointerenter and pointerleave behaviour that closes when leaving trigger and submenu, removed the interaction gap, and retained keyboard and touch behaviour. New navigation tests check destination coverage, category balance, disclosure semantics and breakpoint safeguards.
changes.impact: All thirteen Research destinations, seven Explore destinations and other global links remain exposed on desktop and mobile; the site links were not renamed or removed. Hover-only opening is restricted to fine-pointer desktop devices, while native detail disclosures and accessible focus indicators remain. Real-device screen-reader, Mac Safari and landscape touch testing remain outstanding; automated link and layout-source checks do not replace that review.

changes.title: The Fall of Samaria and Assyrian succession
changes.summary: Published eight documented comparison cases over four teaching-order stages with twelve biblical reading routes, five directly identified RINAP editions, a clearly labelled Shalmaneser V specialist synthesis, edition-specific uncertainty and provenance, an accessible progressive phase filter and offline JSON. Added six mapped historical sections, six anchored claims and five institutional source records, raising the curated source library to 124 and the independent review queue to 72.
changes.impact: Samaria history is not reduced to an invented single siege account. The Bible names Shalmaneser V in the siege narrative while royal Sargonic inscriptions claim conquest. The Pekah/Hoshea killing verb is broken, Sargon deportation totals differ across exemplars, and Sargon annal restorations are distinguishable from preserved signs. Direct citation checks and automated validation do not substitute for independent historical, Assyriological or biblical specialist review.

changes.title: Royal inscriptions and biblical cross-verification
changes.summary: Published six source-scoped comparisons across three edited royal inscription identities and a separately identified Lachish relief, with ten precise biblical reading routes. Added three institutional original-language edition records, direct links and source mappings to four historical article sections, and four anchored claim reviews bringing the pending queue to sixty-six. A dedicated reading room, offline JSON, reciprocal article links, CI regression coverage and documented roadmap accompany the release.
changes.impact: The Bible is cited as primary evidence for its own statements, and royal inscription editions are direct evidence for their commissioned Assyrian claims. RINAP 3 Q003496 explicitly reports 800 silver talents where 2 Kings 18 reports 300; a shared 30 gold figure does not resolve the difference. Royal annals and palace reliefs have separate purposes, and automated tests of source coordinates do not constitute independent historical, biblical or epigraphic review.

changes.title: Ancient names and historical identity disambiguation
changes.summary: Published eight source-scoped person and place evidence dossiers with twelve checked citations to the existing accessioned-object concordance and biblical primary passages. Added a dedicated research room, site-wide and reciprocal navigation, an offline dossier dataset, negative source/approval regression tests, and root/subpath build validation.
changes.impact: A source relationship or similar name is not an independently proven historical identity. Biblical accounts remain primary for what Scripture states; object catalogues and original-language readings have different evidentiary roles. All identity dossiers remain awaiting qualified independent scholarly review, and no new unverified inscriptions or physical object attestations were invented.

changes.title: Ancient text concordance and biblical cross-reference index
changes.summary: Twenty-five manually curated research terms link thirty-two specific tablet or object evidence relationships, forty-three encyclopaedia reading routes and eleven biblical passage comparisons. A locally searchable, accessible concordance hub, direct line anchors, reciprocal article links, offline data export and source/verse validation make these connections navigable.
changes.impact: Relationships distinguish direct edited inscriptions, object-level context, related articles and biblical primary-text comparisons. Similar names or subjects do not establish identical historical people or events. Automated checks cannot replace independent Assyriological, biblical or accessibility review; no such completion is claimed.

changes.title: Ancient text and translation comparisons
changes.summary: Seven source-edited Middle Assyrian tablets now show sixteen tiny, attributed sign-sequence excerpts with line references, original editorial English reading cues and uncertainty notes. Two catalogue-only objects remain without invented ancient-language text; an original five-section methods chapter, three new scholarly notation sources and nine queued claims complement the text-comparison reading room.
changes.impact: The source publication, attribution and CC BY-SA 3.0 terms are visible. Transliteration snippets are distinguished from normalized Akkadian, scholarly translations and independent sign collation; historical and philological verification remains outstanding for all new claims. No image copies, unauthorized full translations or fictitious readings have been included.

changes.title: Individual tablet and archaeological case files
changes.summary: Nine original accessioned object studies with catalogue and CDLI/edition identity, findspot and dating disclosures, line-scope metadata, eight new curated institutional source references, 36 new mapped research sections, 12 anchored claims and a dedicated public object case-file room.
changes.impact: Eight Middle Assyrian objects and one separately labelled later Babylonian Chronicle are connected to their institutional records. A catalogue match is not an independent translation, complete biography or specialist philological review; all new claims remain unreviewed. Museum images and scholarly text editions have not been copied.

changes.title: Middle Assyrian social history and everyday life
changes.summary: Nine new original research guides with 45 section-specific reading trails, ten specialist institutional and academic source records, fourteen anchored claims awaiting review, a social-history research hub and a provincial timeline entry.
changes.impact: Law codes remain normative rather than proof of universal actual practice. Administrative and archaeological archives describe selectively documented households and institutions. Biblical passages are used as separately dated primary texts for their own accounts, not as Middle Assyrian contemporary administrative records. No independent specialist sign-off, object-level line collation or permissions for third-party imagery is claimed.

changes.title: Historical and biblical evidence dossier expansion
changes.summary: Eight new original Bible-primary historical dossiers with 40 source-mapped sections, six museum and inscription-corpus reference records, twelve text-anchored verification claims and a browseable research hub.
changes.impact: Scripture is primary for statements about the biblical account, while accessioned objects and royal inscriptions are separately labelled historical witnesses. These are curated research routes, not independent specialist approval or a verified line-by-line transcription of ancient documents.

changes.title: Source integrity and accessibility audit
changes.summary: Added structural citation validation for curated source records, bounded monthly/manual external URL checks, a public audit page and machine-readable offline index, automated accessible-markup regression tests, corrected keyboard menu handling and accessible atlas status text.
changes.impact: External URLs have not been certified live by the offline build; monthly HTTP probes require human interpretation. Manual device, contrast, screen-reader, Syriac shaping, subject-expert verification and release indexing reviews remain outstanding.

changes.title: Publication stewardship and preservation integrity
changes.summary: Added full generated-site SHA-256 manifests, strict file-integrity verification, deterministic ZIP export with tested recovery, public stewardship guidance and stronger root, subpath and deployment checks.
changes.impact: Fixity does not prove historical truth or provide an independent offsite backup. Actual custodianship, accessibility review, source link maintenance, independent specialist review and search-indexing approval remain outstanding.

changes.title: Public editorial governance and revision history
changes.summary: Added public corrections and review policy, role disclosures, a curated merged-commit register and blank editorial planning worksheets.
changes.impact: No secure private correction intake, appointed specialist reviewer or confirmed public correction case is claimed. This milestone implements editorial infrastructure, not independent historical adjudication.

changes.title: Community testimony and heritage research
changes.summary: Added the public heritage reference room, six original source-mapped articles and blank private-first planning worksheets.
changes.impact: The catalogue links to externally published records; no new private interview content, audio or release forms were collected.

changes.title: Language and script reference expansion
changes.summary: Added eight source-linked language studies and a Unicode-anchored Syriac letter reference room.
changes.impact: Letter identities are validated; pronunciation and original manuscript images remain externally linked or under future expert review.

changes.title: Historical atlas evidence and uncertainty
changes.summary: Added per-stage reconstruction limits, source-scope notes and routes to historical articles across eleven atlas stages.
changes.impact: Map polygons remained schematic and unchanged, and specialist geographic review remains outstanding.

changes.title: Historical encyclopaedia depth expansion
changes.summary: Added fourteen historical reading guides, original sections and section-level bibliographic trails.
changes.impact: Academic and biblical references were linked, but independent specialist verification and inscription-level comparisons remain outstanding.

correction_policy: A dated public correction record is created only after a specific published problem and editorial action are documented. Pending private reports and sensitive personal information must not be published. Substantive corrections should retain a link to the affected article, the evidence and a dated immutable commit; unresolved issues must not be labelled resolved.

statuses.feature-release: A merged website or content delivery, not specialist validation.
statuses.correction: A publicly documented substantive change to a published error, with its limits and supporting source trail.
statuses.clarification: A publicly documented substantive qualification that does not necessarily assert previous text was false.
statuses.withdrawal: An explicit notice that affected editorial material should no longer be relied on.
